title: 【8/22 20:00より販売開始】
summary: Here is how I brew it 僕ならこう淹れる
transcript_original:
【8/22 20:00より販売開始】

「Gakuyuini Kenya Mix varietal Washed」

ケニア中央部に位置するケニア山(キリニャガ)の麓のマイクロファーマーたちによるミックスロットです。品種はSL28, SL34, Ruiru11。どれもケニアを代表する研究品種ですね。

あぁケニアのみたいなぁってなるときがあるんですよ。
夏ってだいたい毎日そんな感じ。もうすぐ夏終わるけど。

そんなケニアですが、あえてクリーンな感じを楽しむのではなくじゅわっといろんな味が溢れるように少しだけ細かめ×長めの抽出時間で成分を出しまくるのがいいと思います。ちょっと濃く仕上がると思うので好みで加水するのもありです。

さらに、細かめでサクサクっと注いだらジューシーでギュッと詰まったタイトな酸をしっかり抽出しやすいと思いますし、粗めでお湯を乗せるように優しく注いだらボリューミーな甘さも表現できると思います。

今回のベースレシピはあくまでベースレシピ。
好みで細かくしたり粗くしたりして調整してみてください。
人の数だけ好みのケニアがあるはずです。
あなたの好みに仕上がりますように。

トマトとかカシスみたいなギュンギュンケニアが好きな人は細かく攻めた抽出に、シトラスとかブラウンシュガーみたいな柔らかほっこりケニアが好きな人は粗く穏やかな抽出に。

兎にも角にも、暑い日に飲みたいケニアです。

Here is how I brew it 僕ならこう淹れる
粉量13g / 中挽き(Comandante 24click±2) / 92℃
0:00-0:07 40g
0:40-0:47 100g
1:20-1:27 150g
2:00-2:07 200g
2:25-2:35 finish

君ならどう淹れる？
飲んでみた感想もお待ちしています。
transcript_en:
[Sales start from 8/22 20:00]

"Gakuyuini Kenya Mix varietal Washed"

This is a mixed lot produced by micro-farmers at the foot of Mt. Kenya (Kirinyaga) located in central Kenya. The varieties are SL28, SL34, Ruiru11. All of them are research varieties that represent Kenya.

There are times when I feel like it's like Kenya.
It's like that almost every day in summer. Summer will be over soon though.

In Kenya, instead of trying to enjoy a clean taste, I think it would be better to extract the ingredients a little finer and with a longer extraction time so that the various flavors are overflowing. I think it will end up a little thicker, so you can add water if you like.

Furthermore, I think that if you pour it finely and crisply, it will be easier to extract the juicy, tightly packed, tight acid, and if you pour it coarsely and gently, as if pouring hot water, you will be able to express a voluminous sweetness.

This base recipe is just a base recipe.
Please try adjusting it by making it finer or coarser as you like.
There are probably as many Kenyans as there are people who like it.
I hope it turns out to your liking.

If you like crunchy Kenyan flavors like tomatoes or cassis, try a finely extracted extraction, while if you like soft, warm Kenyan flavors like citrus or brown sugar, choose a coarser and gentler extraction.

Kenya is the perfect drink on a hot day.

Here is how I brew it
Powder amount 13g / Medium grind (Comandante 24click±2) / 92℃
0:00-0:07 40g
0:40-0:47 100g
1:20-1:27 150g
2:00-2:07 200g
2:25-2:35 finish

How would you brew it?
We look forward to hearing your impressions after trying it.

Pour speed is also important, but the key here is to control the extraction efficiency by creating a phase where you pour the liquid after it has completely drained, and a phase where you pour before the liquid has completely drained.

You can control it in the same way with other recipes, so please give it a try.

グランハパライソの甘さと発酵の香り、そして滑らかな質感をいい感じに出すならこんな多投レシピがおすすめ。

粗挽きに対してサクサク小分けにして注ぐことで水に溶けやすい成分を抽出しつつ、水に溶けにくい成分もこそぎ落としていくイメージかな。

もっと極端に粗挽きにしてもっと細かく注ぎ分けるレシピも面白いけど、いつものレンジでやるならまずはこれで。

普通にいれてもきれいな味わいが楽しめるこのコーヒーの質感をもっとより良くしたいならこのレシピを試してみてね
transcript_en:
Recent trending multi-throw recipes

---This extraction recipe--
　
@rikuto.co
Colombia Granja Paraiso92 Yellow Typica Honey

Powder amount 13g Total pouring amount 200g Water temperature 90℃
Medium coarse grind (Comandante 28click)
　
①0:00-0:05 30g
②0:30-0:35 60g
③1:00-1:05 90g
④1:30-1:35 120g
⑤1:50-1:55 150g
⑥2:10-2:17 200g
2:35 finish

ーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーー
　
If you want to bring out the sweetness, fermented aroma, and smooth texture of Granjaparaiso, we recommend this multi-throw recipe.

I imagine that by pouring coarsely ground powder into crispy portions, the ingredients that are easily soluble in water can be extracted, while also scraping off the ingredients that are less soluble in water.

It would be interesting to have a recipe for grinding it more coarsely and pouring it out more finely, but if you want to do it in a regular microwave, this is the way to go.

If you want to improve the texture of this coffee, which has a beautiful taste even when brewed normally, try this recipe.

title: Granja Paraiso92 Colombia Yellow Typica DAT Honey
summary: Thick-bodied recipe for a complex Colombian honey-process coffee, aiming at tropical fruit and texture.
transcript_original:
「Granja Paraiso92 Colombia Yellow Typica DAT Honey」

コロンビア南西部、カウカに位置するGranja Paraiso92のYellow Typicaをリリースします。

生産者のWilton Benitez氏は先進的なプロセスを行う生産者として有名な、いわばパイオニア的存在。Granja Paraiso92の魅力は、複雑なプロセスとそこから来る味わいに詰まっています。

Honeyと記載していますが、厳密には「Double Anaerobic Fermentation Thermal shock Honey」詳しいプロセスはインポーターであるHaiz coffee importさんのサイトにアクセスすれば見ることができるので、興味のある方はぜひ。

ここでは、このコーヒーの抽出やその先の楽しみ方にフォーカスしていきます。

香り、味わい、口当たり、どれをとってもとにかく厚みのある印象。特に口当たりは素晴らしいものです。あえて酸味を集中的に狙わずとも表現できる熟したトロピカルフルーツのテイストが印象的な一杯でした。

フレーバーは表現しやすいように感じたので、今回はより質感重視のとろっとほわっとレシピで淹れていきます。

いい感じに淹れられると、一口目からツルッととろっとした感じのトロピカル柔らかコーヒーに仕上がります。是非試してみてください。

Here is how I brew it 僕ならこう淹れる
粉量13g / 中粗挽き(Comandante 28click) / 92℃
0:00-0:07 30g
0:30-0:37 60g
1:00-1:07 90g
1:30-1:37 120g
1:50-1:57 150g
2:10-2:17 200g
2:30-2:40 finish

君ならどう淹れる？
飲んでみた感想もお待ちしています。
transcript_en:
"Granja Paraiso92 Colombia Yellow Typica DAT Honey"

We are releasing Yellow Typica from Granja Paraiso92 located in Cauca, southwestern Colombia.

The producer, Mr. Wilton Benitez, is famous as a producer who uses advanced processes, and is a pioneer so to speak. Granja Paraiso92's charm lies in its complex process and the flavor that comes from it.

Although it is written as "Honey", strictly speaking it is "Double Anaerobic Fermentation Thermal shock Honey".If you are interested, you can see the detailed process by visiting the importer Haiz coffee import's website.

Here, we will focus on the extraction of this coffee and how to enjoy it beyond that.

The aroma, taste, and texture all leave an impression of depth. Especially the taste is wonderful. It was an impressive cup with a taste of ripe tropical fruit that could be expressed without trying to concentrate on sourness.

I felt it was easy to express the flavor, so this time I'm going to brew it with a melty and fluffy recipe that focuses more on texture.

When brewed properly, you'll end up with a soft, tropical coffee that's smooth and smooth from the first sip. Please try it.

Here is how I brew it
Powder amount 13g / Medium coarse grind (Comandante 28click) / 92℃
0:00-0:07 30g
0:30-0:37 60g
1:00-1:07 90g
1:30-1:37 120g
1:50-1:57 150g
2:10-2:17 200g
2:30-2:40 finish

How would you brew it?
We look forward to hearing your impressions after trying it.

title: Las Nubes Guatemala Bourbon Washed
summary: Clean, acid-forward pour-over for a washed Guatemala, with slower later pours to preserve citrus clarity.
transcript_original:
「Las Nubes Guatemala Bourbon Washed」

グアテマラの首都からそう遠くない生産地アンティグア。火山に囲まれたこのエリアで栽培を行うPedro 氏が運営するLas Nubes。今回はBourbon種のWashedプロセスです。

まずこのコーヒーを一口飲んだ時に印象的だったのは主張されすぎない柑橘類の酸質。穏やかです。すごく穏やかです。全体的にボリューム感は控えめな割に甘さと酸の印象はしっかり残る。洗練された印象を感じるコーヒーだと思います。

派手なコーヒーが飲みたい、フレーバーがわかりやすいやつが飲みたい、そんな方にはこちらはあまりおすすめできませんが、とにかくクリーンで馴染んでくるようなコーヒーを求めてる方には是非おすすめさせていただきたいコーヒー。

このコーヒーの繊細な酸質を抽出でうまく表現できるなら…

なので今回は酸を主体にさせるレシピで、このコーヒーのキャラクター表現を狙っていこうと思います。味わいは良い感じにクリーンになってくれると思うのであえてのガンガンいこうぜレシピで調整してみました。

前半は太めのお湯でしっかり注いで後半は遅めのお湯で優しく注ぐレシピです。何なら後半は湯音を落としてもいいかもしれません 

Here is how I brew it 僕ならこう淹れる
粉量13g / 中細挽き(Comandante 23click) / 92℃
0:00-0:05 30g
0:45-0:50 100g
1:30-1:40 150g
2:00-2:10 200g
2:20-2:30 finish

 
君ならどう淹れる？
飲んでみた感想もお待ちしています。
transcript_en:
"Las Nubes Guatemala Bourbon Washed"

Antigua is a production area not far from the capital of Guatemala. Las Nubes is run by Mr. Pedro, who grows in this area surrounded by volcanoes. This time it is the Washed process of the Bourbon variety.

When I first took a sip of this coffee, what struck me was the not-too-overpowering citrus acidity. It's calm. It's very calm. Overall, the volume is modest, but the impression of sweetness and acidity remains. I think this coffee gives off a sophisticated impression.

I don't really recommend this for people who want fancy coffee or something with an easy-to-understand flavor, but I definitely recommend it to people who are looking for a clean, easy-to-appeal coffee.

If the delicate acidity of this coffee can be expressed well through extraction...

So this time, I'm going to try to express the character of this coffee with a recipe that uses acid as the main ingredient. I thought the taste would be nice and clean, so I decided to make some adjustments to the recipe.

The first half of the recipe is a thick pour of hot water, and the second half is a slow pour of hot water. If anything, it might be a good idea to tone down the sound of the hot water in the second half.

Here is how I brew it
Powder amount 13g / Medium fine grind (Comandante 23click) / 92℃
0:00-0:05 30g
0:45-0:50 100g
1:30-1:40 150g
2:00-2:10 200g
2:20-2:30 finish

 
How would you brew it?
We look forward to hearing your impressions after trying it.

title: Coffee Tasting Basics
summary: Short tasting-language primer about sweetness, acidity, bitterness, comparison tasting, and using simple descriptors first.
transcript_original:
COFFEE TASTING BASICS

Start with how we taste
The basics of sweetness, acidity and bitterness.

Use the flavour wheel
Start broad before chasing exact flavours.

Build a common language
Find simple words you can return to.

Taste in comparison
Try coffees side by side.

Describe it to someone else
Saying it out loud helps lock it in.

You do not need to find “strawberry cordial with a roasted hazelnut finish” straight away.
Fruity is a great start. Sweet is a great start. Build the language, then build the detail.

とにかく綺麗で華やかなエチオピアウォッシュト
フローラルで甘い香りが特徴の綺麗めコーヒーだよ。
オンラインストアにもまだ若干のこってるけど今回で一旦今の生豆在庫は終了。
また次の入荷は未定だから気になる人はぜひ[rikuto.co]をチェック🔥
transcript_en:
Ethiopian food tastes good, isn't it?

---This extraction recipe--
　
@rikuto.co
Ethiopia Goro Bedessa WS Heiroom Washed

Powder amount 13g Total pouring amount 200g Water temperature 90℃
Medium grind (@comandantegrinder 26clicks)
　
①0:00-0:10 40g
②0:40-0:47 120g
③1:20-1:27 160g
④1:50-2:00 200g
2:40 finish

(This time it didn't fall completely, so I added a little water to adjust the concentration)

ーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーー
　
You'll want to always have a clean Ethiopian wash.
If I can't decide when I go to a coffee shop, I might just order something.

I wanted to enjoy a different floral and bright sweetness from the previous Sour Gyun Gyun recipe, so this time I used a slightly coarser and longer extraction method, and slightly increased the amount of the first shot to enhance the impression of sourness.

Anyway, beautiful and gorgeous Ethiopian wash
It's a beautiful coffee with a floral and sweet aroma.
There are still some items in the online store, but this time, the current stock of raw beans has ended.
Also, the next arrival is undecided, so if you are interested, please check out [rikuto.co] 🔥

title: オレッチはこう淹れる
summary: Hybrid Switch recipe for a fermented natural, using open and close stages to balance structure and fermentation.
transcript_original:
オレッチはこう淹れる

ーーー今回の抽出レシピーーー
　
@brewmethods
Colombia Las Flores Java Natural

粉量 13g 総注湯量 200g 湯温 ①②90℃ ③75℃
挽目 中粗挽（@comandantegrinder 28clicks)
　
①0:00-0:07 30g (open)
②0:40-0:47 90g (open)
③1:20-1:27 200g (close)
2:00 open
2:25 finish 

ーーーーーーーーーーーーーー
　
今回もスイッチを使ったハイブリッドメソッド

なんだけども付けるドリッパーはフラットボトムドリッパーのオレア

コーヒーベットを低くした上でスイッチ機能を使えるからバチバチ発酵系のコーヒーにはすごく向いてるんじゃないかな。

いつもとほとんど同じレシピで発酵系のコーヒーをバランスよく淹れられるから結構重宝しそう。

This is how to brew Orecchi

---This extraction recipe--
　
@brewmethods
Colombia Las Flores Java Natural

Powder amount 13g Total pouring amount 200g Water temperature ①②90℃ ③75℃
Medium coarse grind (@comandantegrinder 28clicks)

Hybrid method using a switch this time too

The dripper I use is Olea, a flat bottom dripper.

Since you can use the switch function while lowering the coffee bed, I think it is very suitable for highly fermented coffee.

It seems to be quite useful because you can make well-balanced fermented coffee using almost the same recipe as usual.

It looks like it will be released in Japan soon, so be sure to get it and give it a try.

title: STOP BUYING DRIPPERS. BUY FILTER PAPER!
summary: Most people think the dripper is doing all the work. But filter paper can completely change the cup.
transcript_original:
STOP BUYING DRIPPERS. BUY FILTER PAPER!

Most people think the dripper is doing all the work.

But filter paper can completely change the cup.

Cafec has three papers that are worth knowing:

T90 is the safe middle ground. Balanced, easy, hard to mess up.

T83 gives you more body.

T92 slows things down for a cleaner cup with more flavour clarity. Perfect for darker roasts or those super funky anaerobics that need a little calming down.

Before you buy your fifth dripper, try changing the paper.

Save the money. Spend it on coffee you actually want to brew.

What paper are you using at the moment? 👇

@elysiaholmes
@cafec_japan

#coffee #filtercoffee #coffeetips #homebarista #specialtycoffee #cafec

title: イエメンのコーヒーはこんな感じで淹れたい
summary: Switch recipe for Yemen coffee with open and close phases and lower first temperature to preserve origin character.
transcript_original:
イエメンのコーヒーはこんな感じで淹れたい

ーーー今回の抽出レシピーーー
　
@the_mocha_lab
Yemen The Premium Gift of Haraz 

粉量 13g 総注湯量 200g 湯温 ①②88℃ ③75℃
挽目 中粗挽（@pietrogrinders @strive_coffeeroasters #9)
　
①0:00-0:07 30g (open)
②0:40-0:55 100g (open)
③1:20-1:35 200g (close)
2:20 open
3:00 finish 

ーーーーーーーーーーーーーー
　
透過と浸漬を使い分けられるスイッチだからこそできるドリップレシピ

円錐でやるとコーヒーパックの嵩が増えてより複雑な味になると思うから、より複雑な味わいにしたいならそっちを選んでもいいかもね。

僕の味覚ではイエメンらしさを楽しむなら程よい軽さもあったほうがいいから今回はウェーブフィルターを選んだよ。

ウェーブフィルターでコーヒーベットの嵩を低くしてサクッと作ることでイエメンらしいテイストと飲みやすいバランスを両立できたので、まずはここからやってみるのがおすすめ。
transcript_en:
This is how I want to brew Yemeni coffee.

---This extraction recipe--
　
@the_mocha_lab
Yemen The Premium Gift of Haraz

Powder amount 13g Total pouring amount 200g Water temperature ①②88℃ ③75℃
Medium coarse grind (@pietrogrinders @strive_coffeeroasters #9)
　
①0:00-0:07 30g (open)
②0:40-0:55 100g (open)
③1:20-1:35 200g (close)
2:20 open
3:00 finish

ーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーー
　
Drip recipes that can only be made with a switch that can use transmission and immersion

I think that if you use a cone, the bulk of the coffee bag will increase and the flavor will be more complex, so if you want a more complex flavor, you may want to choose that.

To my taste, if you want to enjoy the Yemeni flavor, it's better to have just the right amount of lightness, so this time I chose a wave filter.

By using a wave filter to reduce the bulk of the coffee bed and make it crisp, we were able to achieve both a Yemeni taste and an easy-to-drink balance, so we recommend trying this first.
